resposta: Because a catenary riser requires space to develop a sag envelope and to route away from subsea assets, a very small free area around the FPSO reduces the available clearance for riser sag, curvature radii, and avoidance of obstacles. Movement of the hull amplifies the riser envelope, increasing collision/entanglement risk with subsea templates, manifolds, and the FPSO leg / mooring area. With constrained free space, routing, installation tolerances, and inspection/maintenance access become impractical, making catenary solutions more prone to contact, fatigue and re-routing challenges compared with alternatives that require less seabed clearance and simpler routing.
